Where it is used: `config/eval_gpt2*.py` for baselines, `config/finetune_shakespeare.py` for finetuning, and `sample.py --init_from=gpt2-xl` to generate directly.

**Flow: Finetune GPT-2 XL on Shakespeare from OpenAI's weights** (trigger: `python data/shakespeare/prepare.py`, then `python train.py config/finetune_shakespeare.py`.)

1. **Tokenize Shakespeare with GPT-2's tokenizer** [`data/shakespeare/prepare.py:19-30`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/data/shakespeare/prepare.py#L19-L30) Unlike the character version there is no `meta.pkl`: the ids are GPT-2 BPE ids, 301,966 for training.
2. **The config asks for GPT-2 XL and a tiny, constant learning rate** [`config/finetune_shakespeare.py:10-25`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/config/finetune_shakespeare.py#L10-L25) 20 iterations of 32,768 tokens at a constant 3e-5, saving only when validation improves.
3. **train.py hands over to from_pretrained** [`train.py:181-188`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L181-L188) Only dropout is passed through; the architecture values are then read back from the loaded model so the checkpoint records them.
4. **Pick the shape by name** [`model.py:215-225`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L215-L225) `gpt2-xl` means 48 layers, 25 heads, 1600 channels. Vocab 50257, context 1024 and biases on are forced because that is how OpenAI trained them.
5. **Build an empty nanoGPT and list its tensors** [`model.py:230-235`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L230-L235) The causal-mask buffer is skipped because it is not a learned weight.
6. **Download the Hugging Face model** [`model.py:237-239`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L237-L239) `transformers` fetches and caches the checkpoint; its mask buffers are filtered out too.
7. **Copy tensors, transposing the Conv1D ones** [`model.py:241-259`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L241-L259) OpenAI stored four kinds of linear weights transposed (as "Conv1D"). Every other tensor is copied as is, and every shape is asserted to match.
8. **Optionally shrink the context** [`train.py:189-192`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L189-L192) If you pass a `block_size` below 1024, `crop_block_size` cuts the position table [`model.py:195-204`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L195-L204). The finetune config keeps 1024, so nothing changes.
9. **Train as usual** [`config/finetune_shakespeare.py:16-21`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/config/finetune_shakespeare.py#L16-L21) 1 sequence per micro-batch × 32 accumulation steps × 1024 tokens keeps memory per micro-step small. If you still run out of memory, the README suggests a smaller GPT-2 or a shorter `block_size` [`README.md:166`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/README.md#L166).
10. **Sample with GPT-2's decoder** [`sample.py:69-74`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/sample.py#L69-L74) `python sample.py --out_dir=out-shakespeare` finds no `meta.pkl` in `data/shakespeare`, so it encodes and decodes with tiktoken.

> **Checkpoint:** You add a new learnable tensor to `CausalSelfAttention`, then run with `init_from='gpt2'`. Where does it fail?
> - In tiktoken
> - At the assertion that nanoGPT and Hugging Face have the same number of keys
> - In the optimizer
> - Nowhere; the new tensor just stays random
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>At the assertion that nanoGPT and Hugging Face have the same number of keys. The key lists are compared before any copying [`model.py:248`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L248). A new parameter adds one key per layer on nanoGPT's side only.</details>

## Data and state

### Token files and the memmap batch sampler

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** `train.bin` and `val.bin` are headerless arrays of uint16 ids. `get_batch` maps the file into memory, picks `batch_size` random offsets, and copies out windows as inputs and one-token-shifted targets.

By the end you can read and write nanoGPT's data format yourself and say what one batch costs.

**Format.** There is no format: `np.array(ids, dtype=np.uint16).tofile(path)` writes 2 bytes per token, back to back [`data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py:48-52`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py#L48-L52). Nothing in the file records the dtype; you have to know it. `np.fromfile` or `np.memmap` with `dtype=np.uint16` reads it back. OpenWebText is too big to build as one list in memory, so its script creates the output file as a writable memmap of the final size and fills it shard by shard [`data/openwebtext/prepare.py:59-74`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/data/openwebtext/prepare.py#L59-L74).

**Reading a batch.** `get_batch(split)` does four things.

1. Opens the right file as a read-only memmap: a file you can index like an array, where the OS reads only the pages you touch [`train.py:119-122`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L119-L122).
2. Draws `batch_size` random start positions anywhere below `len(data) - block_size` [`train.py:123`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L123).
3. Copies `data[i:i+block_size]` for x and `data[i+1:i+1+block_size]` for y, converts them to int64 (what `nn.Embedding` and `cross_entropy` expect) and stacks them [`train.py:124-125`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L124-L125).
4. On CUDA, pins the CPU memory so the copy to the GPU can run asynchronously [`train.py:126-128`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L126-L128).

**Cost.** One GPT-2 micro-batch touches 12 windows of 1,025 tokens, about 24 KB of a 17 GB file. Windows start anywhere, mid-word and across document boundaries; in OpenWebText the end-of-text token marks those boundaries.

**Why reopen it every call.** Keeping one memmap open let resident memory grow towards the size of the whole file over a long run; reopening it per batch fixed that at negligible cost [`train.py:117-118`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L117-L118) (`5156fef`).

### The checkpoint dict and resuming a run

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** `ckpt.pt` is one dict: model weights, AdamW state, the architecture (`model_args`), the iteration, the best validation loss and every setting. `init_from='resume'` rebuilds the run from it; `sample.py` uses only the weights and the architecture (and the dataset name).

By the end you know what is in `ckpt.pt`, what resuming restores, and two oddities to watch for.

**What is saved.** At an evaluation that passes the save test, the main process writes [`train.py:277-284`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L277-L284):

- `model`: every weight, as a state dict (name → tensor).
- `optimizer`: AdamW's two running averages for every weight, plus its step counts. This is the bulky part. For GPT-2 124M the notebook estimates 1.49 GB for weights plus optimizer, against a real file of 1,542,470,366 bytes [`transformer_sizing.ipynb:136-140`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/transformer_sizing.ipynb#L136-L140).
- `model_args`: the seven `GPTConfig` values.
- `iter_num` and `best_val_loss`.
- `config`: every simple setting, from `dataset` to `learning_rate` [`train.py:76-78`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L76-L78).

**Resuming.** `--init_from=resume` loads the file, forces the six shape values (`n_layer`, `n_head`, `n_embd`, `block_size`, `bias`, `vocab_size`) to match the checkpoint while letting `dropout` follow your flags, loads the weights and the optimizer state, and continues counting from `iter_num` [`train.py:158-180`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L158-L180). It then sets `checkpoint = None`; before that fix (`4ac2e8c`), the loaded tensors stayed alive and resuming could run out of GPU memory [`train.py:200-202`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L200-L202).

**Oddity 1: `_orig_mod.`.** With `torch.compile` on, saved keys look like `_orig_mod.transformer.h.0.…`. Both loaders strip the prefix, under a comment admitting the cause was unknown [`train.py:172-177`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L172-L177). The likely cause: `raw_model` is the compiled wrapper, which keeps the real model in an attribute named `_orig_mod` (inferred).

**Oddity 2: the "best" loss.** With `always_save_checkpoint = True`, the default, every evaluation saves and overwrites `best_val_loss` with the current value, better or worse [`train.py:274-275`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L274-L275). Only with `False`, as in both Shakespeare configs, does `ckpt.pt` hold the best model.

> **Checkpoint:** You resume with `--init_from=resume --n_layer=24` from a 12-layer checkpoint. How many layers does the model have?
> - 24
> - 12: resume overwrites the shape settings with the checkpoint's model_args
> - A type error stops the run
> - Whatever train.py's default is
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>12: resume overwrites the shape settings with the checkpoint's model_args. The six shape keys are copied from the checkpoint over whatever you passed [`train.py:164-167`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L164-L167); only settings like dropout follow your flags.</details>

## File by file

### model.py, top to bottom

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** `model.py` reads in the order it builds: small layers first, then the config, then `GPT` with its forward pass and five utilities. Knowing which block of lines is which tells you where any change goes.

By the end you can open `model.py` and jump to the right 20 lines for any question. Line ranges, and what you would change there:

- **18–27** `LayerNorm`: change the normalisation, for example to RMSNorm.
- **29–76** `CausalSelfAttention`: positions inside attention, caching, masking.
- **78–92** `MLP`: the activation or the 4× width.
- **94–106** `Block`: how the two sub-layers are arranged.
- **108–116** `GPTConfig`: add an architectural setting.
- **118–168** `GPT.__init__` and `_init_weights`: modules, weight tying, initialisation.
- **170–193** `GPT.forward`: the loss or the outputs.
- **195–261** `crop_block_size` and `from_pretrained`: loading other checkpoints.
- **263–287** `configure_optimizers`: weight-decay groups or another optimizer.
- **289–303** `estimate_mfu`: the GPU that MFU is measured against.
- **305–330** `generate`: the sampling strategy.

Four facts that cut across the table:

- Nothing in `model.py` reads files, settings or environment variables. Everything arrives through `GPTConfig` or method arguments, which is why `bench.py` can drive it with random data [`bench.py:44-48`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/bench.py#L44-L48).
- `configure_optimizers` takes `device_type` only to decide on fused AdamW [`model.py:280-285`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L280-L285).
- `estimate_mfu` divides by an A100's 312 TFLOPS [`model.py:299-302`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L299-L302); on any other GPU the percentage is relative to an A100.
- `generate` is wrapped in `@torch.no_grad()` [`model.py:305-306`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L305-L306), so calling it mid-training builds no gradient graph. Call `model.eval()` first, as its docstring advises, or dropout stays on while you sample.

### train.py, section by section

*standard · 6 min*

**In short:** `train.py` is a script of eight sections run in order: defaults, overrides, device and DDP setup, the batch function, model creation, optimizer and compile, two helpers, and the loop. Only three of its pieces are functions.

By the end you know where in `train.py` to make a change and what the change can depend on.

1. **Defaults** (lines 33–74): every setting as a global, with GPT-2 124M values [`train.py:33-34`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L33-L34).
2. **Overrides** (76–78): `configurator.py` runs, then `config` is snapshotted.
3. **Setup** (81–112): DDP or single process, tokens per iteration, `out_dir`, seed, TF32, the autocast context [`train.py:101-102`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L101-L102).
4. **Batches** (114–131): `get_batch`, the whole data pipeline.
5. **Model** (133–193): read `meta.pkl`, then one of three branches, `scratch`, `resume` or `gpt2*`, then an optional crop and `.to(device)` [`train.py:146-149`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L146-L149).
6. **Optimizer, compile, DDP** (195–212). The optimizer is created from the plain model before `torch.compile` and DDP wrap it; the wrappers share the same parameter tensors, so it keeps working afterwards.
7. **Helpers** (214–247): `estimate_loss`, `get_lr`, optional `wandb.init`.
8. **Loop** (249–333), and `destroy_process_group()` at the end for DDP.

Because it is a script, the helpers read globals directly: `estimate_loss` uses `model`, `eval_iters`, `ctx` and `get_batch` from module scope [`train.py:214-228`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L214-L228). That is convenient, and it means you cannot import `train.py` from another file without running a training job.

**Adding a setting** is one line in section 1. If its default is an int, float, bool or string, it becomes overridable with `--name=value` and is saved in every checkpoint's `config` automatically [`train.py:76`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L76). A setting whose default is `None` or a list is left out of `config`, and a `None` default cannot be overridden from the command line at all.

### The supporting files: what to open for which job

*deep · 4 min*

**In short:** Everything outside `model.py` and `train.py` is short and single-purpose: a sampler, a settings snippet, a benchmark, three data recipes, seven config files and two notebooks of arithmetic.

By the end you know which small file to open for a given job.

- **Generate text**: `sample.py`, 89 lines. All its knobs are globals at the top: `init_from`, `out_dir`, `start`, `num_samples`, `max_new_tokens`, `temperature`, `top_k`, `seed`, `device` [`sample.py:12-22`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/sample.py#L12-L22).
- **Understand an override error**: `configurator.py`, 47 lines, executed rather than imported.
- **Measure speed**: `bench.py`, 117 lines. A GPT-2 124M-shaped model, 10 warm-up and 20 timed steps, ms/iter and MFU at the end, CUDA only [`bench.py:100-117`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/bench.py#L100-L117).
- **Prepare your own data**: copy `data/shakespeare_char/` for character-level text, `data/shakespeare/` for small data with GPT-2 tokens, or `data/openwebtext/` for a large Hugging Face dataset.
- **Pick settings**: `config/` holds 7 assignment files. `train_shakespeare_char.py`, `train_gpt2.py` and `finetune_shakespeare.py` are full recipes; the four `eval_gpt2*.py` files differ only in `init_from` and a comment [`config/eval_gpt2_xl.py:8`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/config/eval_gpt2_xl.py#L8).
- **Estimate cost before training**: `transformer_sizing.ipynb` (parameters, checkpoint size, FLOPs, days of training) and `scaling_laws.ipynb` (compute-optimal model size). Nothing runs them; they are worked arithmetic with saved outputs.

What is missing is also information: no `requirements.txt` or `setup.py` (the README's `pip install` line is the dependency list), no tests, and no CI configuration.

## How it was built

### Rebuild it yourself: the order to write nanoGPT

*standard · 7 min*

**In short:** Build it in the order data flows: a prepare script, a batch sampler, the four layer classes, the GPT, the training loop, sampling, and only then the speed and scale features. Each milestone ends with something you can run and check.

By the end you have a plan for writing your own nanoGPT, with a check at every stage. The milestones below each come with a hands-on task.

The order follows the dependencies. Data comes first because nothing in it depends on the model. The model comes before the loop because the loop calls it. Speed features come last because none of them changes *what* is learned: `torch.compile`, mixed precision, Flash attention, fused AdamW and DDP can each be switched off and the code still trains [`train.py:70-74`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L70-L74). The repo's history agrees: the first commit already had a working model, loop and sampler (`fe80428`), and much of the speed work (Flash attention, fused AdamW, vocabulary padding) came about five weeks later.

Three checks catch most mistakes early.

1. **Shapes.** Every block maps `(B, T, C)` to `(B, T, C)`. Assert it.
2. **Initial loss.** A fresh model should score about ln(vocab_size), 4.17 for 65 characters. Far above means bad initialisation. Far below means the model can see its targets, usually a broken causal mask [`model.py:68`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L68).
3. **Overfit one batch.** Train on a single fixed batch for a few hundred steps; the loss should head towards zero. If it does not, the bug is in the loop or the gradients, not the data.

Reference numbers while you build: the baby GPT is 6 layers × 6 heads × 384 channels with dropout 0.2 [`config/train_shakespeare_char.py:21-25`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/config/train_shakespeare_char.py#L21-L25), and the README's results to compare against are 1.4697 validation loss on a GPU or about 1.88 with the small CPU settings.

For a guided version, the README points to Karpathy's "Zero To Hero" video series, whose GPT episode builds this model step by step [`README.md:226`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/README.md#L226).

> **Checkpoint:** Your from-scratch character model's very first validation loss is 0.3. What is the most likely bug?
> - The learning rate is too high
> - The causal mask is broken, so positions can see the tokens they should predict
> - The vocabulary is too small
> - Dropout is too high
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>The causal mask is broken, so positions can see the tokens they should predict. An untrained model cannot beat a uniform guess, ln(65) ≈ 4.17, unless the answer leaks into the input. In GPT the only thing that hides the future is the mask [`model.py:68`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L68), or `is_causal=True` on the fused path.</details>

### How nanoGPT grew: nine busy weeks, then fixes

*deep · 5 min*

**In short:** Most of nanoGPT was written between 28 December 2022 and mid-February 2023, in public, with commit messages that explain each change. After that it took contributor fixes until it was marked deprecated in November 2025.

By the end you can read the git log as a design document, and you know which parts are oldest.

The first commit is titled "first very bad commit" and already contains the shape of today's repo: a 267-line `model.py`, a 191-line `train.py`, `sample.py` and the OpenWebText preparation (`fe80428`). Within two days came the configurator, a benchmark script, DDP and resuming. `torch.compile` was turned on by default on day three, for "almost 1.8X improvement in throughput" (`5a725d9`).

January 2023 made it usable by others. Character-level Shakespeare and the baby-GPT config arrived on 11 January (`d17350a`), and the next commit begins "oh no nanoGPT is trending" (`bb49751`). Weight tying, gradient accumulation and multi-node instructions followed.

Late January to early February was the speed push, each change with a measurement in its message: grad clipping (`3cb3fc0`), the GPT-2 initialisation, optional biases at "about 6% faster" (`e808a67`), Flash attention (`ae06d0b`), fused AdamW (`e170e40`), prefetching (`3fd4c0c`) and the vocabulary padding to 50,304 for "about 25% faster" (`77e7e04`) [`model.py:111`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L111).

From March 2023 the log is mostly merged pull requests (across the whole history, 36 people besides Karpathy wrote 48 commits): device handling, Windows and macOS fixes, the `np.memmap` leak (`5156fef`) and a non-zero first learning rate (`dc81cb3`) [`train.py:233-234`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L233-L234).

The last commit, on 12 November 2025, adds the deprecation note [`README.md:9`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/README.md#L9) (`3adf61e`).

Reading tip: `git log --format='%h %s' -- train.py` gives you the reason behind almost every line, because Karpathy wrote his reasoning, doubts included, into the messages.

## Why it's like this

### Why it is built this way: fewer lines over convention

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** Most of nanoGPT's unusual choices trade conventional structure for fewer lines: globals instead of a config object, `exec` instead of argparse, memmap slicing instead of a DataLoader, an attribute toggle instead of `no_sync()`. Each is documented in a commit or a comment, often with the author's own doubts.

By the end you can explain the repo's odd-looking choices as deliberate, and say what each costs.

The goal is in the README: plain, readable code, with `train.py` as "a ~300-line boilerplate training loop" and `model.py` as "a ~300-line GPT model definition" [`README.md:13`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/README.md#L13). Every decision below serves that line count.

**Settings as globals.** Instead of a config class or argparse, defaults are module variables and `configurator.py` is `exec`'d into them. The docstring calls it "Probably a terrible idea" and gives the reason: no `config.` prefix on every variable [`configurator.py:12-14`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/configurator.py#L12-L14).

**No DataLoader.** Batches are random slices of one memmapped file, prefetched while the GPU works. The commit asks "who needs a dataloader?" (`3fd4c0c`) [`train.py:114`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L114).

**No context manager for DDP accumulation.** The loop sets `require_backward_grad_sync` directly, because `no_sync()` "bloats the code and forces us to repeat code" [`train.py:294-298`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L294-L298).

**One file per role.** The whole model is in `model.py` and the whole loop in `train.py`; there is no `utils.py`, no trainer class, no callbacks. To change behaviour you edit the loop.

The common cost: these choices make the code easy to read and hard to reuse. You cannot import `train.py`, configure it from another program or test parts of it in isolation. That fits a repository meant to be read and forked. The decision records below list each choice with its evidence and trade-off, marked documented or inferred.

> **Checkpoint:** Why does `train.py` set `model.require_backward_grad_sync` instead of using DDP's `no_sync()` context manager?
> - `no_sync()` does not exist in PyTorch
> - To avoid wrapping and duplicating the forward/backward code in a `with` block; the comment says `no_sync()` only toggles this same attribute
> - It is measurably faster
> - To support CPU training
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>To avoid wrapping and duplicating the forward/backward code in a `with` block; the comment says `no_sync()` only toggles this same attribute. The comment explains it: Karpathy read the context manager's source, saw it only toggles this variable, and set it directly [`train.py:295-297`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L295-L297).</details>

### Why it is fast: the measured speed changes

*deep · 6 min*

**In short:** nanoGPT's speed comes from a short list of changes, most with a measurement in the commit: torch.compile (~250 → 135 ms/iter), Flash attention, vocabulary padding to 50,304 (~25%), no biases (~6%), fused AdamW, TF32, and overlapping data loading with GPU work.

By the end you can name each speed trick, where it is in the code, and what it bought.

- **`torch.compile`**: one line, `model = torch.compile(model)` [`train.py:204-208`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L204-L208). The README measured ~250 ms to 135 ms per iteration [`README.md:209`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/README.md#L209).
- **Flash attention**: the fused `scaled_dot_product_attention` kernel never stores the T × T score table [`model.py:62-64`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L62-L64) (`ae06d0b`).
- **Vocabulary padding**: 50,257 → 50,304, a multiple of 64, "about 25% faster" because the output layer was "consuming about 40% of latency" (`77e7e04`) [`model.py:111`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L111).
- **No biases**: `bias = False` in `train.py`, measured "about 6% faster" with "identical results" (`e808a67`, `0e90ee9`) [`train.py:56`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L56).
- **Fused AdamW** on CUDA (`e170e40`) [`model.py:280-284`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L280-L284).
- **bfloat16 autocast and TF32** [`train.py:107-112`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L107-L112).
- **Prefetching**: the next batch is sliced while the GPU runs the forward pass (`3fd4c0c`).
- **Last-position-only logits** at inference (`8f85b83`).

**How to measure your own change.** `bench.py` runs the training step alone and prints time per iteration and MFU [`bench.py:112-117`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/bench.py#L112-L117). MFU (model FLOPs utilization) compares the FLOPs your model needs per second, estimated as 6N + 12·L·H·Q·T per token from the PaLM paper, with an A100's 312 TFLOPS peak [`model.py:289-303`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L289-L303). The sizing notebook measured 37% on one A100 for an early configuration, [`transformer_sizing.ipynb:307`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/transformer_sizing.ipynb#L307), and says it would prefer "somewhere around 50%+" [`transformer_sizing.ipynb:330`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/transformer_sizing.ipynb#L330).

Not every switch is free: `bias=False` makes from-scratch models a different shape from OpenAI's, and `compile` adds about a minute at start-up [`train.py:206`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L206).

> **Checkpoint:** Why does padding the vocabulary from 50,257 to 50,304 make training faster, even though it adds work?
> - It reduces the number of tokens
> - GPU matrix kernels run fastest on dimensions that are multiples of 64, and the output layer is the single largest matrix multiply
> - It shrinks the embedding table
> - It turns on Flash attention
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>GPU matrix kernels run fastest on dimensions that are multiples of 64, and the output layer is the single largest matrix multiply. The commit (`77e7e04`) says the last layer consumed about 40% of latency because of its very high channel count; 50,304 is 64 × 786 [`model.py:111`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L111).</details>

## Handle with care

### Handle with care: the traps you will hit first

*core · 4 min*

**In short:** Run scripts from the repo root, add `--device=cpu --compile=False` without an NVIDIA GPU, write floats with a decimal point in flags, and know that the default checkpointing overwrites `ckpt.pt` at every evaluation. There are no tests, and the repo is no longer maintained.

By the end you can avoid the five problems newcomers hit most, and you know where the rest are listed.

1. **Working directory.** `train.py` opens `configurator.py` and `data/<dataset>/` by relative path [`train.py:77`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L77). Run every script from the repo root.
2. **Hardware defaults.** `device = 'cuda'` and `compile = True` [`train.py:72-74`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L72-L74). On a laptop, a Mac or Windows, pass `--device=cpu` (or `mps`) and `--compile=False`.
3. **Typed flags.** `--learning_rate=1` fails: the value parses as an int and the default is a float [`configurator.py:41-42`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/configurator.py#L41-L42). Write `1.0`.
4. **Checkpoint overwrites.** With the default `always_save_checkpoint = True`, every evaluation overwrites `ckpt.pt` and resets `best_val_loss` to the latest value, even if it is worse [`train.py:274-275`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L274-L275). For anything you care about, set it to `False` (the Shakespeare configs do) or save under new names.
5. **Character prompts.** The Shakespeare character model knows 65 characters; a prompt with any other (most digits, accents, braces) crashes `sample.py` with a `KeyError` [`sample.py:67`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/sample.py#L67).

Two background facts. There are **no automated tests**; correctness rests on inline asserts and on the published loss numbers. And the project is **deprecated** in favour of nanochat [`README.md:9`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/README.md#L9), so PyTorch warnings such as the `torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler` deprecation will not be fixed upstream.

The full risk list below adds the smaller ones: approximate logged numbers, `bench.py` needing CUDA, the GPU count that must divide 40, OpenWebText's disk needs and a GELU variant that differs slightly from OpenAI's.

> **Checkpoint:** You train with `max_iters=20000` and leave `always_save_checkpoint` at its default. The loss diverges at iteration 18,000. What is in `ckpt.pt` at the end?
> - The best model seen during the run
> - The weights from the last evaluation, after the divergence
> - Nothing; diverged runs are not saved
> - One checkpoint per evaluation
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>The weights from the last evaluation, after the divergence. With the default, every evaluation saves to the same path [`train.py:286`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L286), so the last save wins. Set `always_save_checkpoint = False` to keep the best.</details>

### Reading the numbers train.py prints

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** Trust the `step` lines, which average `eval_iters` batches per split. The `iter` lines show a one-micro-batch loss estimate, a time that includes evaluation on eval iterations, and an MFU measured against an A100.

By the end you can tell which printed number to use for which decision.

**`step N: train loss X, val loss Y`.** Printed every `eval_interval` iterations by the main process. Each value is the mean over `eval_iters` random batches (200 by default) in eval mode, without dropout [`train.py:216-228`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L216-L228). This is your comparison number between runs. It is still an estimate: batches are random, so two evaluations of the same weights differ slightly. The eval configs raise `eval_iters` to 500 for steadier baselines [`config/eval_gpt2.py:5`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/config/eval_gpt2.py#L5).

**`iter N: loss X, time Tms, mfu M%`.** Printed every `log_interval` iterations.

- *loss* is the loss of the last micro-batch only, multiplied back by `gradient_accumulation_steps`, and computed with dropout on. The code calls it an approximation [`train.py:321-323`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L321-L323). Expect it to jump around.
- *time* is wall-clock time since the previous iteration. On iterations that also ran `estimate_loss`, it includes the evaluation [`train.py:316-319`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L316-L319).
- *mfu* is a running average, starting after 5 iterations [`train.py:324-326`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L324-L326), of FLOPs achieved against a hard-coded A100 peak. On a different GPU, or on CPU, the percentage is not meaningful as is.

**Start-up lines.** `tokens per iteration will be: …` confirms your effective batch [`train.py:101-102`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L101-L102). `number of parameters: …M` excludes the position embedding. `num decayed parameter tensors …` shows the weight-decay split. `using fused AdamW: …` says whether the fast optimizer path is on.

**What "good" looks like.** For the baby GPT, val loss should fall from about 4.2 towards 1.47. For GPT-2 124M on OpenWebText, about 2.85 after 600,000 iterations; OpenAI's own checkpoint scores about 3.11 there.

> **Checkpoint:** Your `iter` loss jumps by ±0.1 from line to line, while the `step` val losses fall smoothly. Which should you use to compare two runs?
> - The `iter` loss, because it is printed more often
> - The `step` val loss, averaged over `eval_iters` batches with dropout off
> - MFU
> - Time per iteration
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>The `step` val loss, averaged over `eval_iters` batches with dropout off. `estimate_loss` averages many batches per split in eval mode [`train.py:219-226`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L219-L226); the `iter` loss is one micro-batch with dropout on.</details>

## Your first changes

### Your first changes, from easy to hard

*standard · 4 min*

**In short:** Seven exercises take you from turning sampling dials to adding rotary embeddings and the repo's first regression test. Each names the files to touch and how to know it worked.

By the end you have a sequence of real changes to make, each building on the previous one.

Do them in order; each one exercises a different part of the code.

1. **Sampling dials** (easy): no code, only flags on `sample.py`. You learn what temperature and top-k do to real output.
2. **Your own text** (easy): a new `data/<name>/` folder copied from the character dataset. You learn the data contract: `train.bin`, `val.bin`, `meta.pkl`.
3. **Best and latest checkpoints** (medium): a few lines in the evaluation block of `train.py`. You fix the `best_val_loss` overwrite listed under Handle with care.
4. **Gradient-norm logging** (medium): one of the README's open to-dos [`README.md:211-220`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/README.md#L211-L220). You learn the clip and step part of the loop.
5. **Tolerant character sampling** (medium): `sample.py`'s encoder. You learn the tokenizer hand-off between scripts.
6. **Rotary position embeddings** (hard): another README to-do, inside `CausalSelfAttention`. You learn attention's shapes well enough to change them.
7. **A regression test against Hugging Face's GPT-2** (hard): the first file in a `tests/` folder. You learn `from_pretrained` and leave the repo safer than you found it.

For every change, keep one fixed baseline: the Shakespeare config with a fixed seed and the same number of iterations. Compare the `step` val loss lines, not the `iter` lines.

## Reference

### Stack

| Technology | Role | Where |
|---|---|---|
| PyTorch | Everything numeric: tensors, the layers in `model.py` (`nn.Linear`, `nn.Embedding`), automatic gradients, the AdamW optimizer, mixed-precision autocast, multi-GPU DDP and `torch.compile`. | [`model.py:14-16`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L14-L16) |
| NumPy | Writes token ids to disk as raw `uint16` arrays and reads random windows back with `np.memmap` without loading the whole file. | [`train.py:120-125`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L120-L125) |
| tiktoken | OpenAI's GPT-2 byte-pair encoding: turns text into ids from a 50,257-entry vocabulary for the `shakespeare` and `openwebtext` datasets, and back into text in `sample.py`. | [`data/shakespeare/prepare.py:19-22`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/data/shakespeare/prepare.py#L19-L22) |
| Hugging Face transformers | Used in exactly one place: `GPT.from_pretrained` downloads OpenAI's GPT-2 checkpoints and copies the tensors into nanoGPT's own `GPT` class. | [`model.py:212`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L212) |
| Hugging Face datasets | Downloads OpenWebText (about 8 million documents) and tokenizes it in parallel with `.map(num_proc=8)`. | [`data/openwebtext/prepare.py:21-27`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/data/openwebtext/prepare.py#L21-L27) |
| torchrun and DistributedDataParallel (NCCL) | `torchrun` starts one Python process per GPU and sets `RANK`, `LOCAL_RANK`, `WORLD_SIZE`; `train.py` wraps the model in `DDP` so gradients are averaged across processes over NCCL. | [`train.py:82-95`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L82-L95) |
| torch.compile and Flash attention | `torch.compile(model)` fuses the model's operations into faster GPU kernels; `F.scaled_dot_product_attention` runs attention with a fused Flash kernel when available. | [`train.py:205-208`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L205-L208) |
| Weights & Biases (wandb) | If `wandb_log=True`, the main process logs train/val loss, learning rate and MFU at every evaluation. | [`train.py:244-247`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L244-L247) |
| tqdm and requests | `tqdm` draws the progress bar while OpenWebText is written to disk; `requests` downloads tiny Shakespeare. `requests` is not in the README's install line; it usually arrives as a dependency of `transformers` or `datasets`. | [`data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py:12-17`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py#L12-L17) |
| Jupyter, matplotlib, pandas | Only for `scaling_laws.ipynb` and `transformer_sizing.ipynb`, which do paper-and-pencil maths about model size, FLOPs and compute budgets. Not needed to train. | [`scaling_laws.ipynb`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/scaling_laws.ipynb) |

### Files

- [`model.py`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py): The whole GPT in one file: layers, the GPT class, GPT-2 weight import, optimizer grouping, MFU estimate and the sampling loop.
- [`train.py`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py): The training script: settings, single-GPU or DDP setup, batching, model creation, the loop, evaluation and checkpoints.
- [`sample.py`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/sample.py): Generate text from your checkpoint or from an OpenAI GPT-2 model.
- [`configurator.py`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/configurator.py): Not a module: a snippet that `train.py`, `sample.py` and `bench.py` `exec` to overwrite their global settings from argv.
- [`bench.py`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/bench.py): A stripped-down training loop that measures time per iteration and MFU, optionally under the PyTorch profiler.
- [`data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py): Character-level tiny Shakespeare: download, build a 65-character vocabulary, write train/val `.bin` and `meta.pkl`.
- [`data/shakespeare/prepare.py`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/data/shakespeare/prepare.py): Tiny Shakespeare tokenized with GPT-2's BPE, for finetuning GPT-2.
- [`data/openwebtext/prepare.py`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/data/openwebtext/prepare.py): Download OpenWebText (about 8M documents), tokenize with GPT-2 BPE in parallel and write a 17 GB `train.bin`.
- [`config/train_shakespeare_char.py`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/config/train_shakespeare_char.py): Settings for the baby character-level GPT: 6 layers, 6 heads, 384 channels, context 256, 5,000 iterations.
- [`config/train_gpt2.py`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/config/train_gpt2.py): The GPT-2 (124M) reproduction: about 0.5M tokens per step, 600,000 steps, 300B tokens, wandb on.
- [`config/finetune_shakespeare.py`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/config/finetune_shakespeare.py): Finetune GPT-2 XL on BPE Shakespeare: 20 iterations at a constant learning rate of 3e-5.
- [`config/eval_gpt2.py`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/config/eval_gpt2.py): Evaluate OpenAI's GPT-2 (124M) on OpenWebText and exit. Siblings `eval_gpt2_medium.py`, `eval_gpt2_large.py` and `eval_gpt2_xl.py` differ only in `init_from`.
- [`transformer_sizing.ipynb`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/transformer_sizing.ipynb): Back-of-the-envelope maths for GPT-2 124M: parameter count, checkpoint size, memory share, FLOPs per forward pass, MFU and training time.
- [`scaling_laws.ipynb`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/scaling_laws.ipynb): An attempt to reproduce the Chinchilla scaling-law results, used as a rough guide to choosing model and data size for a compute budget.
- [`README.md`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/README.md): The user manual: install, quick start on GPU/CPU/Mac, GPT-2 reproduction, baselines, finetuning, sampling, troubleshooting.

### Glossary

- **Token**: The unit of text the model reads and writes, stored as an integer id. [`data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py:23-31`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py#L23-L31)
- **Vocabulary size (vocab_size)**: How many different token ids exist; it sets the size of the embedding table and of the output layer. [`train.py:153-155`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L153-L155)
- **Context length (block_size)**: The maximum number of previous tokens the model can look at when predicting the next one. [`model.py:170-174`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L170-L174)
- **Embedding**: A learned list of numbers (a vector) for each token id, looked up from a table. [`model.py:126-129`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L126-L129)
- **Residual stream**: The running vector for each position that every block reads from and adds its result back into. [`model.py:103-106`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L103-L106)
- **LayerNorm**: Rescales each vector to mean 0 and variance 1, then applies a learned gain (and optional bias). [`model.py:18-27`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L18-L27)
- **Causal self-attention**: Each position gathers information from earlier positions, weighting them by how relevant they look, and never from later ones. [`model.py:52-76`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L52-L76)
- **Attention head**: One independent attention computation over a slice of the vector; several run side by side. [`model.py:56-59`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L56-L59)
- **MLP (feed-forward)**: A small two-layer network applied to each position separately, after attention. [`model.py:78-92`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L78-L92)
- **Logits**: One raw score per vocabulary entry; higher means the model thinks that token is more likely next. [`model.py:184-187`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L184-L187)
- **Cross-entropy loss**: The average of minus the log of the probability the model gave to the correct next token. [`model.py:187`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L187)
- **Weight tying**: The input embedding table and the output layer share one weight matrix. [`model.py:133-138`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L133-L138)
- **AdamW**: The optimizer: it moves each weight against its gradient, scaled by running averages of the gradient and its square, and shrinks large weights slightly (weight decay). [`model.py:268-275`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L268-L275)
- **Learning-rate schedule**: How big the optimizer's steps are at each iteration: ramp up, then glide down. [`train.py:230-242`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L230-L242)
- **Gradient accumulation**: Run several small batches, add up their gradients, then take one optimizer step, as if it had been one big batch. [`train.py:290-305`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L290-L305)
- **Mixed precision**: Do most of the maths in 16-bit numbers for speed while keeping the weights in 32-bit. [`train.py:109-112`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L109-L112)
- **GradScaler**: Multiplies the loss by a large factor before backward so tiny float16 gradients do not round to zero, then divides it back out. [`train.py:195-196`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L195-L196)
- **DDP (DistributedDataParallel)**: Several processes, one per GPU, each training a full model copy on different batches and averaging gradients. [`train.py:82-91`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L82-L91)
- **Temperature**: A dial for randomness when sampling: below 1 sharpens the probabilities, above 1 flattens them. [`model.py:317-318`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L317-L318)
- **Top-k sampling**: Only the k most likely next tokens are allowed; the rest get probability zero. [`model.py:319-322`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L319-L322)
- **MFU (model FLOPs utilization)**: What fraction of the GPU's peak arithmetic speed the training run is actually using. [`model.py:289-303`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/model.py#L289-L303)
- **Checkpoint**: A snapshot of the model and optimizer saved to disk so training can resume or the model can be sampled. [`train.py:276-286`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L276-L286)
- **Memory-mapped file (memmap)**: A file you index like an array; the operating system reads only the pages you touch. [`train.py:116-122`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/train.py#L116-L122)
- **Finetuning**: Continue training a model that already learned general language, on your own smaller dataset, with a small learning rate. [`config/finetune_shakespeare.py:10-25`](https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT/blob/3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291/config/finetune_shakespeare.py#L10-L25)
